meta.title: Korean Alphabet (Hangul)
meta.subtitle: The 40 letters of hangul — start here, before any word
meta.desc: The first thing to learn in Korean, before any word: hangul, the alphabet King Sejong's scholars promulgated in 1446, in which every syllable is a block of letters (한 = ㅎ + ㅏ + ㄴ). 40 notes, one per letter in use, each with TWO cards (hangul → romanization, romanization → hangul), each scheduled on its own: the fourteen basic consonants, the five doubled (tense) ones, the ten basic vowels and the eleven compound vowels. The romanization is the Revised Romanization of Korean, the official system, and a consonant whose sound changes at the end of a syllable gives both (ㄱ is g, and k at the end). Each card gives the letter's Korean name or how a vowel is written on its own, and a word from the Stage A–C decks that begins with the letter, with its romanization and meaning. Study before Stage A. — Example words: the National Institute of the Korean Language's vocabulary list for learners (KOGL Type 1), meanings from English Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0) and KRDict (NIKL, CC BY-SA 2.0 KR).
